title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 275
paragraphs: Now when they come to the city of Bubastis they do as follows. They sail in boats, men and women together — a great crowd of each sex in every boat; and some of the women have rattles and rattle with them, while some of the men play the flute during the whole of the voyage, and the rest, both women and men, sing and clap their hands. And when, as they sail, they come opposite to any city on the way, they bring the boat to land, and some of the women continue to do as I have said, others cry out and jeer at the women in that city, some dance, and some stand up and pull up their garments. This they do at every city along the river-bank. When they come to Bubastis they hold festival, celebrating great sacrifices, and more wine of grapes is consumed at that festival than during the whole of the rest of the year. To this place (so the natives say) they come together year by year, to the number of seventy myriads of men and women, besides children.
